bib.title: SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
bib.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 16 (2002) 321-357 (submitted 09/01; published 06/02)

question: Can over-sampling the minority class with synthetic examples, combined with under-sampling the majority class, build better classifiers on imbalanced data (in ROC space) than plain under-sampling, Ripper loss-ratio variation or Naive Bayes prior variation?
hypothesis: Synthetic minority examples interpolated between nearest neighbours widen the minority decision region, whereas replication shrinks it, so SMOTE plus under-sampling should beat plain under-sampling and cost-based methods.
contributions: SMOTE: over-sample the minority class by creating synthetic examples along line segments joining k minority-class nearest neighbours
Show SMOTE combined with majority under-sampling gives better ROC-space performance (AUC and ROC convex hull) than plain under-sampling, Ripper loss ratio and Naive Bayes priors on nine datasets
SMOTE-NC for mixed continuous/nominal features, and a proposed SMOTE-N for nominal features (not evaluated)

method.summary: SMOTE creates synthetic minority samples by interpolating between a minority sample and one of its k=5 minority nearest neighbours (gap uniform in [0,1] per sample). ROC curves are built by fixing a SMOTE amount and sweeping majority under-sampling; C4.5, Ripper and Naive Bayes are compared with 10-fold CV, AUC by trapezoid rule and ROC convex hull.
method.task: binary classification on imbalanced tabular datasets

datasets.name: Adult
datasets.preprocessing: for SMOTE only the continuous features were extracted; SMOTE-NC used all

datasets.name: E-state
datasets.source: NCI Yeast AntiCancer Drug Screen, Tripos E-state descriptors

datasets.name: Satimage
datasets.preprocessing: smallest of 6 classes as minority, rest collapsed

datasets.name: Mammography
datasets.split: 10-fold CV; training folds about 9831 majority and 233 minority

datasets.name: Can
datasets.source: Can ExodusII data via AVATAR / Mustafa tool

other.priors: minority prior varied from 1 to 50 times the majority class

training.objective: C4.5 / Ripper / Naive Bayes fitted on the resampled training set
training.regularisation: C4.5 pruning used (Fig 4 reports pruned tree size); C4.5/Ripper hyperparameters otherwise not stated

other.smote_amounts: minority over-sampled at 50%, 100%, 200%, 300%, 400%, 500% (1 to 5 curves per dataset, fewer for less skewed data)
other.undersample_amounts: majority under-sampled at 10%, 15%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 300%, 400%, 500%, 600%, 700%, 800%, 1000%, 2000% (varied per dataset; 5% to 2000% for Mammography plain under-sampling)
other.undersample_definition: under-sampling at 200% means the modified set has twice as many minority as majority elements
other.resampling_inside_folds: inferred: Mammography training folds quoted as about 9831 majority / 233 minority, so resampling is applied to training folds only

inference.samples: 10-fold cross-validation; %TP and %FP averaged over the 10 folds; no repeats or seeds stated

parameters.N_percent: multiples of 100 (50% handled by random subset of minority samples)

metrics.name: AUC
metrics.definition: area under ROC curve (%FP vs %TP) by trapezoid rule; point (100,100) added if missing; leftmost point is raw-data classifier
metrics.unit: printed as integers such as 9330 (scale not stated; AUC scaled by 10^4 is an inference)

metrics.name: ROC convex hull
metrics.definition: points on the hull (Graham's algorithm) are potentially optimal classifiers; judged by number of hull points per method

metrics.name: Acc+ / Acc-
metrics.definition: accuracy on minority / majority examples (Oil, comparison with Kubat et al.)

baselines: one-sided selection and SHRINK (Kubat et al.; Oil)
eval.protocol: 10-fold CV; ROC per dataset from curves, one to five SMOTE curves per dataset, only the best SMOTE curve is drawn; AUC Table 3 for C4.5 only, none for Ripper or Naive Bayes; no significance tests or variance reported

availability.data: Mammography from http://morden.csee.usf.edu/~chawla (URL as printed); Naive Bayes code from fuzzy.cs.uni-magdeburg.de/~borgelt

evidence.quote: Our implementation currently uses ﬁve nearest neighbors.
AUC's [C4.5 as the base classiﬁer] with the best highlighted in bold.

results.claim: Mammography, C4.5: best SMOTE + under-sampling AUC (400% SMOTE) beats plain under-sampling.
results.setup: Mammography, 10-fold CV, C4.5; 400% SMOTE column vs Under column; best column bold. Other SMOTE amounts: 100%: 9250, 200%: 9265, 300%: 9311, 500%: 9304
results.table: Table 3, row Mammography, columns 400 SMOTE (9330, bold, read from page image) and Under (9260)
results.note: 100% SMOTE (9250) is below plain under-sampling; the gap of 70 points is on the printed integer scale; no variance given. The pdftext drops the 9330 cell position but the number is present in the text.

results.claim: Phoneme, C4.5: best SMOTE + under-sampling AUC (200% SMOTE) vs plain under-sampling.
results.setup: Phoneme, 10-fold CV, C4.5; 200 SMOTE column vs Under; 100% SMOTE gives 8644
results.table: Table 3, row Phoneme, columns 200 SMOTE (8661) and Under (8622)

results.claim: Phoneme: the SMOTE + under-sampling ROC curve dominates the curve from varying C4.5's leaf decision threshold over the whole range; shown only as a figure with no AUC value.
results.setup: Phoneme only, C4.5, leaf thresholds 0.5 down to 0.0 (17 values) versus SMOTE and under-sampling; ROC in %FP/%TP, Fig 24; comparison motivated by Provost (2000)
results.note: Text: "The graph shows that the SMOTE and under-sampling combination ROC curve is dominating over the entire range of values." Qualitative claim from one dataset; the SMOTE amount used in Fig 24 is not stated in the text.

results.claim: Adult with SMOTE-NC (and SMOTE on continuous-only features) performs no better than, and by AUC worse than, plain under-sampling; authors blame high-variance minority continuous features whose synthetic points overlap the majority space.
results.setup: Adult, 48842 samples, 11687 minority; SMOTE-NC (50% SMOTE shown) with C4.5 and Ripper, Figs 26-28; Adult is not in Table 3 so no AUC value is printed
results.note: Quote: "SMOTE-NC with the Adult dataset differs from our typical result: it performs worse than plain under-sampling based on AUC, as shown in Figures 26 and 27." Warning: "Some of the minority class continuous features have a very high variance, so, the synthetic generation of minority class samples could be overlapping with the majority class space, thus leading to more false positives than plain under-sampling." The overlap explanation is a hypothesis, not tested; AUC falls as SMOTE exceeds 50%. Figure captions say curves 'overlap for most of the ROC space'.

results.claim: SMOTE-classifier was not the best in only 4 of 48 experiments.
results.setup: 9 datasets, C4.5 / Ripper / Naive Bayes comparisons judged by ROC convex hull; Pima (Naive Bayes wins), Oil (Under-Ripper wins), Can (curves overlap)
results.quote: Out of a total of 48 experiments performed, SMOTE-classiﬁer does not perform the best only for 4 experiments.
results.note: Judged by hull point counts and curve inspection, not significance tests.

results.claim: Table 3 only shows the best AUC across SMOTE amounts: the paper also states it plots only the best SMOTE curve per dataset.
results.setup: All datasets; one to five SMOTE curves are built and only the best is drawn; Table 3 bolds the best SMOTE amount per row, selected on the same 10-fold CV results used to report it (no held-out selection)
results.note: Quote: "We only show the best results from SMOTE combined with under-sampling and the plain under-sampling curve in the graphs." So yes: the paper reports best curve across SMOTE amounts, which is an optimistic selection.

results.claim: Across datasets the best SMOTE AUC exceeds plain under-sampling, but gaps vary: Pima 7307 vs 7242, Oil 8537 (500%) vs 8524, E-state 6828 vs 6811, Can 9560 (50%) vs 9535; Oil at 200-400% falls below Under.
results.setup: Oil, C4.5, Table 3; 300% SMOTE gives 8161, below Under 8524
results.table: Table 3, row Oil, columns 500 SMOTE (8537) and Under (8524)
results.note: Text claim: for all datasets the combination improves over plain under-sampling, which holds only for the best amount per row.

results.claim: Pima (least skewed): Naive Bayes dominates SMOTE-C4.5 in ROC space; Oil: Under-Ripper dominates SMOTE-Ripper.
results.note: Quote: "for the Pima dataset, Naive Bayes dominates over SMOTE-C4.5; for the Oil dataset, Under-Ripper dominates over SMOTE-Ripper."

results.claim: Over-sampling with replication yields much larger pruned trees and worse minority recall than SMOTE at high amounts (100% to 500%).
results.setup: Mammography, C4.5, 10-fold CV, minority over-sampled 100-500%; Figs 4, 5, 19 (values only in figures)
results.note: Text: tree sizes for replication "are much greater than those for SMOTE". No numeric values in the text.

results.claim: On Oil, SMOTE (500%) with 50-125% under-sampling is comparable to SHRINK and better in some cases, but offers no clear improvement over one-sided selection.
results.setup: Oil, 500% SMOTE, Table 5 vs SHRINK Acc+ 82.5%, Acc- 60.9% and one-sided selection Acc+ 76.0%, Acc- 86.6% (Table 4, reported from Kubat et al. 1998)
results.quote: SMOTE oﬀers no clear improvement over one-sided selection.
results.note: Quote contains no number; value from Table 5, row 50%: Acc+ 89.5%, Acc- 78.9%.

limits: Evaluation is entirely ranking-based (ROC, AUC, hull, Acc+/Acc-); the paper never evaluates predicted probabilities, calibration, Brier score or log loss, and does not discuss that resampling shifts the class prior and so distorts probabilities. The only probability-related item is C4.5 leaf thresholds in Section 5.4.

Best SMOTE amount is chosen per dataset on the same CV results that are reported (Table 3 bold, plotted curves); no held-out selection, no variance, standard errors or significance tests; AUC differences are often small (Oil 8537 vs 8524).
AUC reported for C4.5 only; none for Ripper or Naive Bayes; Adult has no AUC entry in Table 3; the Table 3 scale is not stated.
Threshold comparison (Section 5.4) is on Phoneme only, C4.5 only, graph only.
Binary classes only; SMOTE does not handle all-nominal data; SMOTE-N is proposed but not tested.

SMOTE can fail: Adult (high-variance continuous features, overlap with majority); Can (structural neighbourhood in mesh geometry, so SMOTE amount reduced); Pima and Oil lose to Naive Bayes or Under-Ripper.
Authors concede crowding: a minority sample may have a majority sample as nearest neighbour; adaptive k is future work. Only k=5 is used, no sensitivity analysis.
Dataset counts inconsistent: E-state 53,220 in text vs 46869+6351 in Table 2; Can 443,872 in text vs 435512+8360 in Table 2.
Sampling with majority under-sampling was compared against classic, 2002-era learners only (C4.5, Ripper, Naive Bayes); no modern learners.

terms.definition: over-sampling the minority class by taking each minority sample and introducing synthetic examples along the line segments joining any/all of the k minority class nearest neighbors

Synthetic Minority Over-sampling TEchnique-Nominal Continuous; distance adds the median of minority-class continuous-feature standard deviations for each differing nominal feature; nominal value of synthetic sample is the majority value among the k nearest neighbours
proposed variant for nominal features using the modified Value Difference Metric for neighbours and majority vote for values (not evaluated)
